cards.claim: Graphical (triangle, head-to-tail) addition: place the tail of B at the head of A; the line from the tail of A to the head of B is R = A + B.
cards.quote: To find the sum A + B, we place vector B so that its tail is at the head of the vector A, as in Fig. 3.4(b). Then, we join the tail of A to the head of B. This line OQ represents a vector R, that is, the sum of the vectors A and B.

cards.claim: Vector addition is commutative: B + A gives the same resultant R as A + B.
cards.quote: If we find the resultant of B + A as in Fig. 3.4(c), the same vector R is obtained. Thus, vector addition is commutative:

locator.section: 3.4 Addition and subtraction of vectors — graphical method

cards.claim: Vector addition is associative: adding A and B first and then C gives the same result as adding B and C first and then A.
cards.quote: The result of adding vectors A and B first and then adding vector C is the same as the result of adding B and C first and then adding vector A :
cards.equation: (\vec A+\vec B)+\vec C=\vec A+(\vec B+\vec C)

locator.section: 3.4 Addition and subtraction of vectors — graphical method

cards.claim: Subtracting B from A is defined as adding A and -B.
cards.quote: We define the difference of two vectors A and B as the sum of two vectors A and –B :

locator.section: 3.4 Addition and subtraction of vectors — graphical method

cards.claim: Adding two equal and opposite vectors gives a resultant of zero magnitude, the null (zero) vector.
cards.quote: Since the magnitudes of the two vectors are the same, but the directions are opposite, the resultant vector has zero magnitude and is represented by 0 called a null vector or a zero vector :

locator.section: 3.4 Addition and subtraction of vectors — graphical method

cards.claim: The parallelogram method (tails at a common origin, resultant along the diagonal) gives the same result as the triangle method; the two are equivalent.
cards.quote: In Fig.3.6 (c), the triangle law is used to obtain the resultant of A and B and we see that the two methods yield the same result. Thus, the two methods are equivalent.

locator.section: 3.4 Addition and subtraction of vectors — graphical method

cards.claim: The triangle inequalities for |a+b| and |a-b| hold because a side of a triangle is never longer than the sum of the other two (nor shorter than their difference); equality holds only for collinear vectors.
cards.quote: Hint: The sum (difference) of any two sides of a triangle is never less (greater) than the third side. Equality holds for collinear vectors.

cards.claim: NCERT Example 3.1: rain falls vertically at 35 m/s and wind blows east to west at 12 m/s; find how a boy should hold his umbrella.
cards.quote: Rain is falling vertically with a speed of 35 m s–1. Winds starts blowing after sometime with a speed of 12 m s–1 in east to west direction. In which direction should a boy waiting at a bus stop hold his umbrella ?

cards.claim: Result of NCERT Example 3.1: the umbrella should be held in the vertical plane at about 19 degrees to the vertical, towards the east.
cards.quote: Therefore, the boy should hold his umbrella in the vertical plane at an angle of about 19 o with the vertical towards the east.

cards.claim: Learners confuse the resultant of two velocities (v1 + v2) with the velocity of one object relative to another (v1 - v2); the two must be distinguished.
cards.quote: An object subjected to two velocities v1 and v2 has a resultant velocity v = v1 + v2. Take care to distinguish it from velocity of object 1 relative to velocity of object 2 : v12= v1 − v2.
